label: Kodak T-Max 100
source: Kodak Alaris Inc., KODAK PROFESSIONAL T-MAX 100 Film technical data, KODAK Publication No. F-4016 (February 2016, revised 2-16); curves read from the PDF's vector chart paths (page 8)
notes: Approximate digitization; not supplied or endorsed by Eastman Kodak Company or Kodak Alaris. The page-8 characteristic and spectral sensitivity curves are vector paths in the PDF; curve vertices were read directly from the path geometry (line segments, cubic Beziers sampled at 8 steps; no raster tracing) and axes calibrated on the vector frame and tick marks (log H -4.0..+1.0, density 0..4.0 or 0..3.0; 250-750 nm, log sensitivity -2.0..2.0), then resampled linearly on a 0.02 log H grid (spectral: 1 nm). Characteristic curves (page 8, 'Exposure: Daylight; Densitometry: Diffuse Visual'): three charts, KODAK PROFESSIONAL Developer D-76 small tank 20 C (three curves), T-MAX RS Developer and Replenisher large tank 20 C 8/10.5/13/15 min, and T-MAX Developer small tank 20 C 6/7/10/12 min; all eleven are in all_curves. Curves were matched to their legend entries by the path's dash pattern (solid, long dash, short dash, dash-dot), not by density order. The D-76 chart legend is defective in this PDF: its three entries print only the glyphs 'PL Q' (no time), so the D-76 development times are not stated; those curves are named by line style. channels.k is the D-76 long-dash curve, the lowest-contrast of the three: the image-structure data (granularity, spectral sensitivity) are stated for D-76 at 68 F (20 C), the small-tank starting point is D-76 at 68 F for 6 1/2 min, and the page-9 small-tank contrast-index line for D-76 gives CI 0.58 at 6 1/2 min (line spans 6.3-9.1 min, CI 0.56-0.82). The long-dash curve's contrast index computed from the digitized curve is 0.52-0.55 by the constructions tried, at or just below the line's lower end, while the short-dash curve maps to about 7.4-8.0 min and the solid curve to 9 min or more; this time assignment is an inference, not a printed value. The same CI constructions applied to the labelled T-MAX and T-MAX RS curves differ from the page-9 lines by up to 0.04-0.08, so the inferred D-76 times are uncertain by about 1 min. The T-MAX Developer 12 min curve ends at the chart's top frame (D 3.0, log H 0.39) and is clipped there. x is log H (lux-seconds) as charted. log_h_ref: none. The charts carry no 18% grey, speed-point or normal-exposure mark, so no reference exposure is placed; the text gives ISO 100/21 (EI 100). Spectral sensitivity (page 8): 'LOG SENSITIVITY', sensitivity = reciprocal of exposure (ergs/cm2) required to produce the specified density; effective exposure 1.4 seconds, D-76 at 68 F (20 C), diffuse visual densitometry. Two curves are charted, D = 0.3 and D = 1.0 greater than D-min, both starting at 400 nm (the chart shows no data below 400 nm); channels.k is the D = 1.0 curve (mid-tone level, 400-670 nm), and both are kept in spectral_sensitivity.all_curves. rms_granularity is the printed diffuse rms granularity 8 (net diffuse density 1.00, 48 um aperture, 12x; D-76 68 F (20 C)); no granularity curve is published. Not recorded (no field in this schema): MTF curve (page 8), resolving power (63 lines/mm at TOC 1.6:1, 200 lines/mm at 1000:1), contrast-index curves (page 9, used only for the D-76 time inference), reciprocity, filter-factor and push-processing tables.
